story.value: Gadolinium is named after the mineral gadolinite, where it was found, which was named for the Finnish rare earth chemist Johan Gadolin.
The Swiss chemist Jean Charles Galissard de Marignac first observed spectroscopic evidence of gadolinium in the minerals didymia and gadolinite.
In 1886, the French chemist Paul-Emile Lecoq de Boisbaudran gave the element the name gadolinium.

uses.value: Gadolinium compounds are used to make phosphors for color televisions.
Gadolinium can be combined with yttrium to form garnets used in microwave technology.
Gadolinium can be alloyed with metals such as iron and chromium to improve their workability and resistance to high temperatures and oxidation.
Gadolinium can be used as control rods for nuclear reactors.
